overall: The AG found the Fall River School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by answering a request for executive session minutes within 10 business days instead of the required 10 calendar days; the notice-of-timing allegation was rejected.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to timely respond to a June 11 request for 18 sets of executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the request for minutes was sent to the Committee but the Committee failed to respond within 10 calendar days, instead responding within 10 business days.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to inform him when the requested minutes would be provided to him.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body specifically inform a requestor when minutes will be provided, just that a public body respond to the request within 10 days and either provide copies of the minutes or conduct a review of the executive session minutes if it has not done so already.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements (cautioned that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
